$comment: Per-service memory ceilings for KDE Plasma 6 desktop services.
Why this module exists: 2026-04-28 21:15 KWin OOM-style death from a
2-day-old session. kwin_wayland used 1.1G + 815M swap, plasmashell
used 692M + 983M swap, ksystemstats had a runaway leak (42min CPU,
known KDE 6.2.x bug). When KWin's INTERNAL allocation fails, the whole
Wayland session dies and SDDM kicks back to login. earlyoom would NOT
have helped — it has --avoid for these very services (correct: you
don't want earlyoom killing kwin under any circumstance).
2026-08-07: removed per-service MemoryHigh/MemoryMax drop-ins. They were
an independent hard-cap mechanism competing with the global PSI watchdog
(freeze-guard + systemd-oomd, see aa_desk-usr.../cloud-data-system-protection.json)
— plasma-plasmashell.service's cap alone caused two freeze/crash incidents
via memory.high throttle-thrash (not real OOM, PSI stayed low) before the
thrash-voter's own sustain-counter bug was fixed there. Sole source of kill
decisions is now that one global watchdog; every per-service hard cap found
in the repo is being removed for the same reason (see grep for 'MemoryMax'
across the repo — nothing should hardcode one outside that file).
What this module does now: ONLY proactive self-healing, no kill authority.
watchdog_warn_mb = RSS threshold to proactively restart BEFORE any real
pressure forms (still useful — a clean restart beats
waiting for a PSI kill on a known KDE leak)
watchdog_action  = 'restart' (in-place safe) or 'notify' (kwin: never auto-restart)
Sized for Surface Pro 8 (8GB RAM, 8 logical CPUs).
Adding services is data-driven: edit this JSON, no script change needed.

plasma-kwin_wayland.service._note: Restarting kwin tears the Wayland session — only notify, NEVER auto-restart. No hard MemoryMax — the global PSI watchdog decides if a real kill is warranted.

plasma-plasmashell.service._note: 2026-07-31: this service's own MemoryHigh/MemoryMax caused sustained memory.high direct-reclaim throttle (memory.events high=259229) that froze/crashed the shell twice with no real OOM and low aggregate PSI. 2026-08-07: removed the cap entirely — the global PSI watchdog (with its thrash-voter sustain bug now fixed) is the only kill authority. Plasmashell restart is in-place safe; user sees panel flicker only.

plasma-ksystemstats.service._note: Known leak in KDE 6.2.x — recycle aggressively, no UI impact.

plasma-kded6.service._note: Defense in depth — kded daemons can leak; restart is invisible.
